message.content: {"back_translation":"It was on a lugubrious night of November that I contemplated the accomplishment of my labours. With an anxiety that bordered almost on agony, I gathered around me the instruments of life, in order to breathe a spark of existence into the inanimate thing that lay at my feet. It was already one o'clock in the morning; the rain crackled sadly against the windowpanes, and my candle was almost consumed, when, by the glimmer of that half-extinguished light, I saw the yellow and dull eye of the creature open; it breathed laboriously, and a convulsive movement agitated its limbs.\n\nHow to describe my emotions before this catastrophe, or how to depict the wretch whom, with such infinite pains and cares, I had striven to form? His limbs were well proportioned, and I had chosen his features for their beauty. Some beauty! — Great God! His yellow skin barely covered the network of muscles and arteries beneath; his hair was of a shining black and floating; his teeth of a mother-of-pearl whiteness; but these luxuries formed only a more horrible contrast with his tearful eyes, which seemed almost of the same colour as the dull white sockets in which they were set, his parchment-like complexion and his straight and black lips.","changes":[{"shelley":"dreary","translation":"lugubre","back_translation":"lugubrious","category":"intensification","rationale":"\"Lugubre\" carries funereal, mournful overtones that are stronger than the English \"dreary\", which suggests gloom or bleakness."},{"shelley":"pattered dismally","translation":"crépitait tristement","back_translation":"crackled sadly","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Crépiter\" suggests a sharper crackling sound than \"patter\", and \"tristement\" (sadly) is milder than \"dismally\"; the change could also be read as a softening."},{"shelley":"it breathed hard","translation":"elle respira péniblement","back_translation":"it breathed laboriously","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Hard\" suggests forceful, heaving breath, while \"péniblement\" stresses difficulty and suffering, which gives the creature a more pitiable cast."},{"shelley":"Beautiful!","translation":"De la beauté !","back_translation":"Some beauty!","category":"domestication","rationale":"The French partitive exclamation is an idiomatic way of voicing bitter irony, but it changes the echo of the preceding \"beautiful\" into a noun."},{"shelley":"the work of muscles and arteries","translation":"le lacis des muscles et des artères","back_translation":"the network of muscles and arteries","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Lacis\" gives an anatomical image of interlacing, but it loses \"work\", which hints at the labour of construction and at Frankenstein's own craftsmanship."},{"shelley":"luxuriances","translation":"luxes","back_translation":"luxuries","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Luxuriance\" means lush abundance, whereas \"luxes\" suggests expensive indulgences, so the sense is slightly different."},{"shelley":"watery eyes","translation":"yeux larmoyants","back_translation":"tearful eyes","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Larmoyant\" implies weeping or tearfulness, while the English describes a moist, filmy, pale look; this adds emotion that is not in the original."},{"shelley":"dun white sockets","translation":"orbites d'un blanc terne","back_translation":"sockets of a dull white","category":"softening","rationale":"\"Dun\" implies a dingy brownish-grey, but \"terne\" just means dull, so the specific sickly colour is lost; it could also count as a shift in meaning."},{"shelley":"shrivelled complexion","translation":"teint parcheminé","back_translation":"parchment-like complexion","category":"shift in meaning","rationale":"\"Parcheminé\" is a familiar French image of dry, wrinkled skin, but it is more static than \"shrivelled\", which suggests shrinking and withering."}],"note":"This is a close and fairly literal rendering that keeps the structure, rhythm and sequence of Shelley's sentences. Its changes are mostly small lexical ones, and they pull in different directions: \"lugubre\" is somewhat stronger, while \"tristement\" and \"terne\" are somewhat weaker. Words like \"larmoyants\", \"parcheminé\" and \"lacis\" bring in familiar French images and slightly alter the clinical, repellent description. Judgments about tone rest on a short passage, so they should be taken with caution."}
